F1.statement: For EU accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026, signed Amendment A sets EU retention at 18 months, effective 1 March 2026.
F1.qualifier: Applies only to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026.

F2.statement: For EU accounts opened before 1 January 2026, the EU retention period remains 12 months.
F2.qualifier: Applies only to accounts opened before 1 January 2026.

F3.statement: Standard, non-EU customer data is retained for 24 months after contract termination.

F4.statement: Draft Amendment B is unsigned and not approved; it only proposes 24 months for all EU accounts effective 1 September 2026.
F4.qualifier: It is a draft and not an effective rule.

F5.statement: The public trust page snapshot does not reflect the current EU position; it shows EU accounts at 12 months, and the DPO email states it has not been updated to reflect Amendment A.
F5.qualifier: As of the 18 April 2026 snapshot and the 20 April 2026 DPO email.

F6.statement: The system-of-record export is not current and not controlling for the amended EU cohort; it shows EU retention as 12 months and is stale for accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026, while signed amendments control over operational exports.
F6.qualifier: For EU accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026.

F7.statement: Backups of enterprise customer data are retained for 35 days and are governed separately by the Backup Retention Schedule, not by the Enterprise Data Retention Policy.
F7.qualifier: For backups of enterprise customer data.

F8.statement: Amendment A was signed on 5 May 2026 but is effective from 1 March 2026, so its effective date precedes its signature date.
F8.qualifier: Amendment A applies only to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026.

F9.statement: Two distinct incidents occurred in March 2026: INC-031 and INC-032.
F9.qualifier: In March 2026, as identified by incident timelines and the audit note.

F10.statement: INC-031 occurred on 2 March 2026, lasted 75 minutes from 14:05 to 15:20 UTC, was caused by an expired TLS certificate on the edge gateway with the renewal job not running and the expiry alert disabled, and had 12,400 failed transactions.
F10.qualifier: For INC-031, the duration is the service degradation window from 14:05 to 15:20 UTC.

F11.statement: INC-032 occurred on 4 March 2026, lasted 45 minutes from 09:10 to 09:55 UTC, was caused by a failed rollback of CHG-441 due to an incompatible schema change in the rollback script, and had 3,100 failed transactions.
F11.qualifier: For INC-032, the duration is the service degradation window from 09:10 to 09:55 UTC.

F12.statement: The two incidents together had 15,500 failed transactions, and they did not have the same root cause.
F12.qualifier: Total across INC-031 and INC-032; the audit note identifies separate events with different causes.

F13.statement: The remediation plan is a draft and not approved; the root-cause note recommends automatic certificate rotation, re-enabled expiry alerts, and a weekly certificate inventory check, while the draft plan proposes moving certificate management to the platform team, retiring the current renewal job, and adding a quarterly audit.
F13.qualifier: The plan is not approved; the root-cause note recommendations are separate from the draft plan.
